content.content:
explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh
#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
# The environment is env.sh's, set here without sourcing it, since env.sh also removes parser directories in
# /tmp. The tree is the one this script is in. FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is the pin of build.xml's fastTrack macro,
# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
else
for t in "$@"; do
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit $t"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "$D/$t" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
fi
clean "$@"

## B.6 Type checking

`TypeCheckPhase` builds indexes for the apis and components, checks the apis, then the components (`phases/TypeCheckPhase.java:32-58`); the work is in `StaticChecker.checkCompilationUnit` (`compiler/StaticChecker.java:163`).

For an api: compound-api check, api linking, type-hierarchy acyclicity, well-formedness (`:174-220`).

For a component: `ApiTypeExtractor`, `TypeNormalizer`, a `TraitTable` and a `TypeAnalyzer`, then `Thunker` to give elided return types thunks, then `STypeChecker.typeCheck` (`:196-247`), then well-formedness again, overloading rules, export checking and the variance checker (`:268-290`).

The checker writes a type onto each expression node and produces no new representation, which is why the same `nodes/` tree continues into DESUGAR.

The variance checker is skipped when `compiled_expr_desugaring` is off, with the comment "Hack: don't run the variance checker if running the interpreter" (`StaticChecker.java:289-290`) — one of the few places in the checker that names the interpreter at all.

`Shell.getScala()` selects between the Scala checker and a Java one that no longer exists (`StaticChecker.java:228-230`); `setScala(false)` is set by `walk` (`Shell.java:422`), `typecheck-old` (`:467`), `test` (`:475`), the bare-filename arm (`:481`) and the `-typecheck-java` flag (`:865`).

== explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:365-375

## B.7 Overloading

Resolution is split between a shared rewrite and two completely different dispatch mechanisms.

The shared part: `OverloadRewriter` replaces a reference that has several candidates with a reference to a single synthetic name spelled `f{f1,f2,…}` and appends a `_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` declaring it (`compiler/OverloadRewriter.java:74-92`, `OverloadRewriteVisitor.java:110-142`).

On the interpreter path, `BuildTopLevelEnvironments.for_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` (`interpreter/evaluator/BuildTopLevelEnvironments.java:128`) turns that declaration into an `OverloadedFunction`, and the actual selection happens per call, on run-time values, in `OverloadedFunction.bestMatch` (`interpreter/evaluator/values/OverloadedFunction.java:787`); failure is the familiar "Failed to find any matching overload" (`:795`).

On the compiler path, `CodeGen.for_RewriteFnOverloadDecl` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:6409`) hands the declaration to `OverloadSet`, which emits one dispatch method per overloaded name, testing argument types from most to least specific (`compiler/OverloadSet.java:1944,1964`).

So the same phase feeds a run-time search in one world and a generated decision tree in the other, and the candidate lists they start from are different (`OverloadRewriteVisitor.java:107`): the interpreter's comes from the disambiguator, the compiler's from the type checker.

  choose(self, b: Blue) = "blue"
end

run(): () = do

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
DistanceMulti.java
add-patch.py
classify.py
compare.sh
errors.py
run.sh
shadow-patch.py
table.py
test_classify.py

facts-extract: part 1 of 1. Its 1 part prints 5165 bytes, about 2200 tokens.
Asked for, and where it is:
  doc:explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md#Decisions, findings explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:371-446  [4799 bytes]

== explorations/perf-probes/checker-speed-2/REPORT.md:371-446

## 11. Decisions, findings, questions

**Decisions.** No decision of the curator covers 1 to 6.

1. **The split in order (variant B).** Rejected:
   - variant C, which tests `Node` first and skips 213 tests for leaves: 332 s against B's 344 s, one run
     each, within noise; its exactness needs a proof (every node class implements `Node`);
   - the JVM switch alone: 652 s, and a switch every JVM would need;
   - a class-keyed dispatch.
2. **30 cases per method.** The largest method is 4,474 bytes, against the limit of 8,000.
3. **The patch changes the generator and the file it writes, not the file alone.** A build would otherwise
   regenerate the old walker the next time `Fortress.ast` or a generator changes.
4. **An audit by branch index, not by memo hits.** The fix adds no memo.
5. **The test is in Java**, because of the scalac 2.13 limit (§8).
6. **The brief's "distance stage is `tools/count-run/`" read as `tools/distance/run.sh`.** `count-run.sh`
   runs each interpreter test under walk.

**Findings.**
- The interpreted walker (§2.2).
- The shares of the repair (+267 s) and of rung C (+109 s before the fix, +65 s after) (§3).
- After the fix, about 95 % of the component's time is in the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3).
- The checker's output depends on identity hashes (§9).
- The repair removes the distance stage's crash row and adds no site (§6).
- The other methods over the limit are negligible after the fix (§2.2).

**Defects.**
- **The interpreted walker.** My change repairs it (way 1), pinned by `WalkerJUTest`. No ledger row holds it;
  the row to write:
  - claim: the generated `Walker.walk` (`FortressAst.scala`, from `ScalaAstGenerator.java`) is 31,704 bytes
    of bytecode, past HotSpot's 8,000-byte huge-method limit, so the JVM never compiles it, and every phase
    that walks a tree runs it in the interpreter;
  - status: NEGATIVE-VERIFIED, closed by the fix's commit;
  - class: implementation gap (generator, speed);
  - spec: silent;
  - reproducer: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`;
  - found by: this probe.
- **The identity-hash dependence.** A note for row 488, with the H runs' commands and outputs (§9).

**Sentences of the specification made false:** none.

**For FACTS.**
1. **The fact.** The generated AST walker's `walk` was one method over HotSpot's 8,000-byte limit, so it ran
   interpreted. With it split in order, the count stage with row 680's repair takes 352 s instead of 911 s,
   and the distance stage 931 s instead of 2,375 s, with identical output.
   - What it means: row 680's line can land under the 690 s rule.
   - Test: `WalkerJUTest.testEveryMethodCompilable`.
   - Detail: §2.2 and §6.
2. **The fact.** The checker's output depends on the JVM's identity-hash sequence, because AST hashes include
   the `Class` identity hash. One extra identity hash at start reorders the api checks and the members of
   unions in messages.
   - What it means: the stages' outputs can move with an unrelated edit (row 488).
   - Command: the driver with `-Dprobe.hashes=1`.
   - Detail: §9.
3. **The fact.** Rung C's normal form costs 12 % of the count stage before the fix, 19 % after.
   - Detail: §3.

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
  message text, once.

**Commands worked out.**
- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
  longer than 8,000 bytes.
- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.

content.content:
See \chapref{trait-parameters} for a discussion of static parameters.
A static parameter may be instantiated with a type or a value
depending on whether it is a type parameter.
\note{
Victor: I don't know if the follow really belongs here.
It isn't complete in any case, because of union/intersection types.}
Two types are identical if and only if they are the same kind and
their names and static arguments (if any) are identical.
Two \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} static arguments
(\secref{natparams}, \secref{static-expr})
are identical if and only if they are written alike
once each operation whose operands are numerals is replaced by its value:
\EXP{2\;3} and \EXP{6} are identical,
and \EXP{s_{0}\;s_{1}} is identical to itself but not to \EXP{s_{1}\;s_{0}}.
Two such arguments are known to differ when they are two different numerals;
a static parameter, or an expression in which one occurs,
is not known to differ from a numeral,
since the parameter may be instantiated with a value at which they are equal.
\revision{revival-sizes}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said only that the
static arguments of identical types are identical, and did not say when two
static arguments written as expressions are. The two sentences above say it,
in the reading of the team's own questions and answers on overloaded operators
in the appendix ``Internal Document'': a numeral differs from another numeral,
and an expression with a static parameter in it is not known to differ from a
numeral.}
Types are related by several relationships as described in
\secref{type-relations}.

Syntactically,
the positions in which a type may legally appear (i.e., \emph{type contexts})
is determined by the nonterminal \emph{Type} in the Fortress grammar,
defined in \appref{concrete-syntax}.

2474:\subsection{Overloading with static parameters}
which it accepted before and whose compiled class then failed verification, and
an override whose return type reorders its static parameters, which it accepted
before and which then failed at run time (row~398).
Neither implementation runs every set these rules allow.
The compiled type checker refuses more than the Return Type Rule where the more
specific declaration's parameter type is an object type, as in
\EXP{\VAR{ident}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON{}T} beside
\EXP{\VAR{ident}(x\COLON \TYP{Circle})\COLON \TYP{Circle}} where \TYP{Circle} is an
object (row~542); the compiled code generator fails on two declarations with
static parameters whose bounds differ, the pair the Return Type Rule allows in
\secref{overloading-static-params} among them, and on the example of the type
group's paper of 2019 that overloads a method over an array list and a list
(row~537); and the interpreter refuses at load two declarations with static
parameters of which no pair of parameter types excludes each other (row~159),
that example among them (row~539), except where a pair of their parameter types
excluded each other only as it read each declaration at one symbolic instance of
its static parameters, shared where both declare the same ones: such a pair it
reads on the two declared domains, each over its own instances, by these rules.
Jan's example is still not a valid overloading, its two declarations having the
same parameter type.
The compiled type checker applies the No Duplicates Rule as it is now stated:
it refuses two declarations whose parameter types, read over their instances,
are each a subtype of the other, ``There are multiple declarations of \VAR{dup}
with the same parameter type'', two functional methods among them wherever their
\KWD{self} parameters stand.
It reads the abstract functional methods that a trait or object provides as it
reads the abstract dotted ones, so that an abstract functional method beside a
concrete one with the same parameter type is among the pairs it refuses, which
only its code generator refused before, as a malformed overload set.
It checks no overloading of an operator whose name is not a word of capitals
(row~584 of the revival's gap ledger): two declarations of such an operator with
the same parameter type pass it, and only its code generator refuses them, as a
malformed overload set (row~726).
The interpreter refuses at load two declarations with static parameters whose
parameter types, each read over its own instances, are each a subtype of the
other, as \VAR{dup}'s are; it loads a declaration whose parameter types are its
static parameters beside one whose parameter types are their bounds, a plain one
(row~549) or one whose parameter types mention none of its static parameters
(row~742), and runs one of the two.
The compiled type checker and the interpreter both refuse two declarations with
static parameters whose parameter types exclude only together, through a static
argument that another parameter's type fixes (row~740), and the compiled type
checker refuses two pairs of declarations with static parameters that the
interpreter loads, one whose parameter types exclude through the one instance
of a supertype they share and one whose static parameters' bounds exclude each
other (row~741).
The calculus of \appref{overloading-calculus} keeps its rule that two
declarations with the same number of parameters have static parameters with the
same bounds; it admits fewer overloadings than these chapters, so that its valid
programs are still valid, and its rules and its soundness claim are unchanged
(\secref{revival-calculi}).

- Original: the No Duplicates Rule, the Meet Rule over what a type provides and the return-type rule read abstract declarations too (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex`; `Specification/basic/traits.tex`). The compiled checker read only functional methods with a body when it checked what a type provides. So these passed the checker:
  - an abstract and a concrete functional method with the same parameter types, in one trait. The code generator then stopped.
  - an object that inherits an abstract functional method from one trait and its body from another, and declares none of its own. It ran the body.
  - an object's functional method that defines its trait's abstract one with an unrelated return type. Its run failed the JVM's verification.
- Resolution: the checker reads every functional method that a type provides, abstract ones too. It refuses the three cases: "There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type", "Invalid overloading of pick in trait O" and "For f, the return type of ... should be a subtype of ...". Walk refused all three at load already. The checker's check of top-level overloads still skips the abstract functional methods of a component's own traits: `h(self): ZZ32` abstract in a trait beside a top-level `h(x: String): ZZ32` passes it (ledger row 739).
- Reason: the specification's rules, and the code generator's own refusal of such a set. The type group's Welterweight calculus refuses the second case too. Scala accepts it, and the revival keeps Fortress's rule.

content.content:
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../explorations/experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT=/home/user/fortress-checkrows/tmp/rung-checker-four-rows/ladder/root
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT=/home/user/fortress-checkrows/tmp/rung-checker-four-rows/ladder
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

The ledger, explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md, is sorted into topic sections,
each a "## TITLE" heading over one table of rows. A row is one line of eight
cells, and keeps its number wherever it sits:

  | # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |

The template (POSITIONS.md, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is
explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md, 4.1):
  status       exactly one of POSITIVE-VERIFIED, NEGATIVE-VERIFIED,
               NEGATIVE-BOUNDED, CONTESTED, RETIRED, FIXED, DUPLICATE
  class        `kind (area)`, kind one of the legend's seven, area one of ten;
               `—` only for POSITIVE-VERIFIED and RETIRED
  spec         the .tex file and the section heading in quotes; a line number
               only against Specification-1.0-frozen/; `silent` where the
               specification does not say
  reproducer   one test (a name under the test folders, or a path) or probe
               path from the repository root, or `none`
  limits       row 1,200 characters, claim 300, reproducer 200, found by 60,
               notes 700
  a pipe inside a cell is written \\|

Cells are split only at a pipe that is not escaped as \\|. A row whose cells
hold bare pipes (the ledger had six) does not split into its table's width that
way; it is read by its split at pipes followed by a space or the line's end, as
facts-extract.py has always read it, and check reports it under `pipe`.

Every write takes a lock (flock on .ledger.lock beside the ledger), checks the
template on the line it writes, and puts the full earlier line of a row it
changes, unchanged, in the history file beside the ledger
(fortress-gap-ledger-history.md), under "### Row N" and a line saying what
became of it. A failed check prints the rules the row breaks and exits 1.

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored
  add FILE --section TITLE   FILE holds one row line, its # cell `?` (or the
                             seven cells after it); numbers it max + 1 and
                             inserts it in that section's table in number
                             order
  note N TEXT                appends TEXT to row N's notes

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

object Ratio(num: ZZ, den: ZZ) extends { QQ }
    getter asString(): String = if den = 1 then num.asString else num.asString || "/" || den.asString end
    getter isNaN(): Boolean = (numerator(self) = 0 AND denominator(self) = 0)

    asFloat(self): RR64 = asFloat(num) / asFloat(den)
